Introduces an unsupervised graph-based method for discovering tissue domains
from multiplexed spatial proteomics data. Cells are represented as nodes in a
joint graph combining marker expression similarity and physical proximity;
community detection over this graph recovers domains that respect both
signal and geography, in contrast to expression-only clustering. The paper's
second contribution is a spatially-constrained permutation null for cell-cell
neighborhood enrichment testing, explicitly contrasted against the
random-labeling null used in most prior work and shown to avoid inflated
significance in tissues with large-scale gradients. Applied to multi-organ
cohorts and validated against independent histological annotation.
